title: Chang'an
subtitle: Imperial capital and meeting point of the three traditions
shortSummary: Chang'an compressed court, state education, monasteries, Daoist institutions, markets and international travellers into one city.
curatorialDescription: Chang'an was not an abstract setting for harmonious coexistence. It was an urban space where institutions, resources, authority and religious networks competed and borrowed from one another.
The map uses a real geographic referent as a schematic. Historical names, institutional identities and building-level locations still require further source-based refinement.
researchNote: This is an Alpha city-level place. Monasteries, Daoist institutions, the Guozijian and translation sites have not yet been modelled as complete institution/place pairs.
